modules.intro: Built from your own sketch. No tutorial part, no step list.
modules.title: The Part
modules.aiNote: Unrestricted for driving SolidWorks. Ask the assistant anything about the program, as often as you want. It will not make design decisions for you, and neither will anyone else, because you have to defend every dimension out loud.

blocks.content:
**1. Attach your part file.** Save as `V1_LASTNAME.SLDPRT` and attach it to this assignment. That file is the real submission. Everything else here is you telling us about it.

**2. Upload one screenshot.** The whole SolidWorks window, so the list of features down the left side is readable. That list is called the FeatureManager tree and it is most of what gets looked at.

**3. Fill the table.** Four rows, one each:

- Anchor hole diameter
- Throat opening width
- Centre to centre
- Thickness

Measure each one on your own model, then look up what the rule says in the guide and put it beside yours.

**Your part is allowed to be illegal today.** Throat came out at 1.180? Centres at 2.640? Write it down. You are not graded on hitting the numbers, you are graded on knowing where you stand. Fixing them is what V2 and V3 are for.

**No mass today.** That number comes from Bambu Studio and you have not been shown it yet.

modules.intro: You named two designs on Thursday. This is where you say what happened to them.
modules.title: What You Took From Yesterday
modules.aiNote: COACH only. Ask it to explain how a feature works. Do not ask it what your design should be.

blocks.content:
On Thursday you wrote down two designs from the case library and what you were taking from each.

Say which one actually made it into your hook, and point at where on the part it is.

**"Neither one" is a full-credit answer** if you say what you did instead and why you changed your mind. Dropping an idea once you start drawing is normal. Saying you used it when you did not is the problem.

blocks.prompt: Which design from Thursday shows up in your hook, and where on the part is it? If neither did, what replaced it and why?

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names a design from Thursday and the specific place on this hook where it appears, or explains a deliberate abandonment with what replaced it.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names a design and says it influenced the part, but does not locate it on the hook.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Talks about being influenced without naming a design or a location.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Blank, or names designs that do not match what this student recorded on Thursday.

rubric.criterion: The answer points at a specific feature on the student's own part

modules.intro: Thirty seconds, and it is worth the same five points however you answer it.
modules.title: What Stopped You
modules.aiNote: No AI. This is a report on your own period and only you were there.

blocks.content:
Something stopped you longer than anything else today. Everybody had one.

Write what it was, roughly how long it cost you, and what finally got you moving: the assistant, a TA, the person next to you, or working it out yourself.

**Say it honestly and you get all five points whatever it says.** This is how we find out whether the assistant and the TAs are actually helping. "Nothing stopped me" tells us nothing and changes nothing about Monday.

columns.tip: Be specific. "SolidWorks was hard" is not an answer.
columns.label: What stopped you

columns.tip: Assistant, TA, neighbour, or figured it out.
columns.label: What got you moving
